what_worked: Power-law framing and median-over-mean advice show genuine statistical awareness worth preserving.
fix_next: Rebuild every number from the assigned 1,000-row dataset; the 8,782-row source invalidates nearly all claims.
verdict: Wrong dataset undermines otherwise reasonable but shallow analysis with decorative filler visuals.
factual_error_detail: Slide 2: 8,782 rows vs required 1,000; 59% Stripe (5,185) vs reference 636/1000=63.6%; 36% country unknown vs 241/1000=24.1%; 22%/1,952 for-sale count not verifiable against 1,000-row set. Slide 4: AI 1,430 listings vs reference 197; SaaS 525 vs 66; median MRR figures ($16.90, $57.10, $20.52) unverifiable against reference medians. Slide 5: B2B median $15.99 / B2C $8.37 not reconcilable with reference. Slide 6: US 1,657, India 807, France 612, UK 603 all from larger dataset. Slide 7: Stripe 5,185, RevenueCat 1,236 vs reference 636 and 189.

evidence.insight: AI-paradox (volume vs revenue quality), B2B/B2C split, and power-law observation are directionally sound ideas but each slide makes one surface-level point with no cross-cutting analysis, no correlation work, no actionable recommendation.
evidence.narrative: Loose topic sequence (overview→distribution→categories→geography→infra→marketplace→takeaways) but no stated thesis, no building argument, and the summary slide merely restates prior slides without synthesis.
evidence.framing: No audience, research question, or scope statement. Missingness is mentioned (36% country unknown) but the percentage is wrong for the assigned dataset. The 8,782 figure suggests the student analyzed a different or full-platform dump rather than the course dataset.
evidence.accuracy: Systematic mismatch: every slide's counts, percentages, and medians correspond to an ~8,782-row dataset, not the 1,000-row assignment. This is the most damaging issue—at least 8 distinct numerical claims cannot be verified against the reference and most are demonstrably wrong for the assigned data.
evidence.visual: Charts are minimal two-bar horizontal bars that restate text. Slide 1 neon dashboard, slide 6 fantasy map, slide 8 AI-generated storefront are purely decorative with no analytical value. No annotations, no multi-variable visualizations, no data-driven color encoding. Gamma template is repetitive.
evidence.ai_slop: Three slides (1, 6, 8) use AI-generated decorative imagery unrelated to the data. Gamma template produces uniform layout with no customization. Callout boxes and numbered takeaways feel templated rather than crafted.
